rv.q: Eclipsed is a major achievement — a scorching work about women and war whose humor burnishes rather than undermines its seriousness of purpose.

Superbly directed by Liesl Tommy and powerfully acted by a strong ensemble led by the Oscar-winning star of '12 Years a Slave,' Lupita Nyong'o, the play gives voice to women ranging from the wives of warlords to activists in Women of Action for Peace.
Under Liesl Tommy's vibrant direction, Eclipsed is a work of profound humanity.
Among its many other virtues, Eclipsed offers the thrill of hearing voices too often drowned out.
For all its harrowing power, 'Eclipsed' shines with a compassion that makes us see beyond the suffering to the indomitable humanity of its characters.
That “Eclipsed” is the Gurira play that made it to Broadway isn’t just history — it’s a promising sign of the future.
Radiant Nyong’o, simplistic drama.
Eclipsed is one of the best plays of the season, infinitely watchable and completely unforgettable.
Liesel Tommy's excellent direction and the playwright's sensitive writing balances each argument evenly, presenting each woman to be heroic, and flawed, in her own way.
Liesl Tommy directs her sensational ensemble with an escalating sense of danger and urgency.
And Zainab Jah, as #2, was a standout even in this distinguished company: kinetically fierce – a knife-edge of a performer who bristles with danger.
"Eclipsed" is a very powerful, resonant play, bringing home what it means to be completely helpless in our world.
But from that uncertainty Gurira has wrenched a dazzling, urgent drama that knows what it is, what it wants, and why it matters—for those suffering no less than its subjects, and everyone else, too.
That they would do so to tell the horrific story of the Liberian Civil War, and its brutal effect on the women who lived through it, is as surprising as it is brave.
It brings the audience uncomfortably close to a destructive environment.
Eclipsed does open a window on a world we rarely get to see this intimately, and they deliver it so gracefully that the play’s flaws feel less consequential than the resonating force of its story.

"What could easily have been a noble, grim and largely unwatchable testament to man’s inhumanity towards woman in wartime turns out to be a well-acted ensemble piece and a thought-provoking drama that is surprisingly vibrant, and sometimes even whimsical...

"Liesl Tommy’s taut staging provides an excellent showcase for the play. The cast is uniformly very good and while performances have deepened and feel more lived-in uptown, there are still few moments—light and serious—when individuals tilt toward being overly showy, as though they’re performing. Despite that, the play is unsettling and eye-opening.
Capturing a sport onstage is tricky and The Royale wisely goes for theatricality.

Eclipsed is precisely the kind of work that precludes this reaction, forcing a confrontation between audience and subject matter without offering the easy pressure relief valve of cynical hopelessness or self-congratulatory liberalism.
The play is edge of your seat suspenseful, yet beautiful, and directed by a South African director who obviously loves the play.
She enlivens the arc giving depth and desire as we watch her breath life into herself.
Except for a few slow moments in the first act, the play is consistently gripping.
“Eclipsed” is a redemptive and salvific story offered with distinctive grace and distinguished craft and not to be missed.
This powerful drama about the resilience of women during Liberia'
I recommend this clearly sincere play to anyone interested in learning more about this underworld activity which becomes only more graphic when put before us on a stage.

The background African rhythms by Broken Chord, colorful palate of Jen Schriever’s lights against Clint Ramos’ scenic design and vibrant costumes all enhance the emotional roller coaster that prevails throughout this two hour and 15 minute masterpiece.
The performances are brilliantly nuanced and paced by Lisel Tommy.

cn.t: Critics praise Danai Gurira's powerful drama about Liberian women during civil war, celebrating its profound humanity, expert tension, and exceptional all-female cast led by Lupita Nyong'o in a stunning Broadway debut.

vs.sum: The John Golden Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, though sound quality can vary, especially under the mezzanine. Seating comfort is typical of older theaters with tight legroom, but the venue maintains a pleasant ambiance overall. Facilities are adequate, though not exceptional.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restroom (use adjacent Schoenfeld).
